label: Used purchase · inspection and release
brief: You act for the buyer. Inspection has finished. The inspection centre identifies an airworthiness discrepancy. The seller refuses to correct it and asks to retain the deposit and positioning costs. Prepare the buyer’s election before the notice window closes.

questions.prompt: Which path fits a refusal by the seller to fix an airworthiness item identified by the named centre?
choices: Reject under the refusal branch and claim the specified inspection and positioning costs
Use ordinary rejection and always bear round-trip movement costs
Accept unconditionally and recover consequential losses under the warranty
questions.value: Reject under the refusal branch and claim the specified inspection and positioning costs
questions.quote: all costs of the Pre-Purchase Inspection attributable to the Acceptance Items
questions.reason: Ordinary rejection and rejection after a refusal have different cost rules. The text limits the latter claim to specified costs.

questions.prompt: How many days after the inspection does the contract give for the written election? Enter the number as drafted.
questions.quote: by use of Exhibit A within 2 (two) days
questions.reason: Section 7 specifies days. The separate balance-payment clause expressly uses business days.

questions.prompt: If the team instead agrees to a cure, which pair of documents should it use, in sequence?
choices: Exhibit A with the outstanding discrepancies, then Exhibit B at delivery
Exhibit B with discrepancies, then the equipment list as final receipt
The two forms are interchangeable once the seller has the funds
questions.value: Exhibit A with the outstanding discrepancies, then Exhibit B at delivery
questions.quote: Subject to Seller's correction of the following discrepancies at Seller's expense
questions.reason: A records technical acceptance subject to identified corrections. B records delivery. Do not sign the receipt while the exception remains unresolved.

proof.prompt: Copy the words in the refusal paragraph that expressly name who pays the specified inspection costs.
proof.start: Should Seller refuse to correct the Airworthy Items
proof.quote: shall be paid for by the Seller, including all positioning expenses
proof.core: shall be paid for by the seller

memo: Serve the written rejection before the election expires and request prompt return of the deposit. Document the centre’s finding and the seller’s refusal. Object to a duplicate positioning deduction under the specific refusal branch and reserve rights over its interaction with ordinary rejection. Itemise eligible costs. Review the conflicting internal references before authorising funds.

label: OEM purchase · which delay remedy governs?
brief: You act for the airline. A slot has slipped. Someone has entered an exact daily recovery into the budget using the first delay clause they found. Read the rest of the filing before approving the entry.

questions.prompt: Which instrument expressly substitutes an entire liquidated-damages provision for the main clause?
choices: Letter Agreement 7, paragraph 3
Exhibit C, the price revision formula
The form of bill of sale
questions.quote: 11.1 of the Agreement is deleted in its entirety
questions.reason: The replacement instruction and the letter’s inconsistency rule establish the route to the controlling text.

questions.prompt: What can the team put in a receivables forecast using this public text alone?
choices: A conditional claim structure with the amount and key time inputs undisclosed
The full purchase price for each delayed aircraft
A zero daily rate because no digits are visible
questions.value: A conditional claim structure with the amount and key time inputs undisclosed
questions.quote: US $[***] (US Dollars – $[***]), for each day of delay
questions.reason: Identify aircraft category, revised contractual month, delay cause, applicable cap and claim procedure. Redactions prevent a numerical entitlement.

questions.prompt: What immediate instruction best protects a potential claim?
choices: Obtain the operative unredacted deadline and serve the required written claim in time
Wait for the seller to pay automatically after technical acceptance
Wait until expiry of every aircraft warranty before sending a claim
questions.value: Obtain the operative unredacted deadline and serve the required written claim in time
questions.section: Letter Agreement 7 ¶3, last paragraph before UNQUOTE
questions.quote: submitting a written claim for liquidated damages to the Seller not later than [***]
questions.reason: Preserve evidence now. A late aircraft alone cannot establish amount, timeliness or coverage.

proof.prompt: Copy the words in the replacement provision that make relief depend on an action by the buyer.
proof.start: The Buyer’s right to liquidated damages in respect of an Aircraft is conditioned on
proof.quote: submitting a written claim for liquidated damages
proof.scope: 11.1 of the Agreement is deleted in its entirety and replaced

memo: Challenge the budget entry. Reconcile the affected aircraft and its revised delivery period to the effective letters, then verify which days qualify and who will send the claim. Obtain the unredacted calculation before booking any particular recovery.

label: Operating lease · the first two rent invoices
brief: You act for the airline. Assume qualifying tender and delivery on the same day, a current payment status with no Default, and 18 qualifying modification days within the first rental period. Use a hypothetical daily rent of $4,000. No alternate application of the credit is agreed.

questions.prompt: What event anchors the defined Rent Commencement Date in this aircraft-specific lease?
choices: Tender under the referenced common-terms clause
First revenue flight
Completion of the post-delivery modifications
questions.value: Tender under the referenced common-terms clause
questions.reason: Read the definition back into §3.2. Condition at delivery and the date of the first revenue flight answer different questions.

questions.prompt: How much credit in dollars accrues on the stated facts?
questions.reason: 18 × $4,000 × 50% = $36,000. The assumed days are within the 30-day limit.

questions.prompt: How should treasury schedule the credit on these facts?
choices: Apply it to rent for the second rental period following delivery
Withhold half of the first invoice before tender
Treat it as an unconditional maintenance reserve refund
questions.value: Apply it to rent for the second rental period following delivery
questions.quote: the second Rental Period following the Delivery Date
questions.reason: When the credit is earned and when it may be used are separate cash events.

proof.prompt: Copy the part of the rent paragraph that says where to apply the credit.
proof.quote: the second Rental Period following the Delivery Date

memo: Verify tender under the incorporated agreement and pay the first instalment as required. Document qualifying work days and check default status. Reconcile the credit to the later invoice. If working capital is tight, request written agreement to earlier application.

label: Finance lease · loss and interim funding
brief: You act for the operator. Assume a qualifying loss of the entire aircraft on day 0 and applicable insurance proceeds paid on day 54. The lessor has not previously received the full amount in a form it can irrevocably apply. The operator proposes stopping rent on day 0.

questions.prompt: By which numbered day must the operator pay or cause payment of the agreed insurance value on the assumed facts?
questions.quote: 90 days after the occurrence of an Event of Loss
questions.reason: The earlier of day 90 and receipt of proceeds on day 54 is day 54. The full-receipt exception has not already discharged the obligation.

questions.prompt: What must the team establish before treating both scheduled rent streams as ended under the loss clause?
choices: Full irrevocable and unconditional payment of the agreed insurance value
An insurance adjuster has opened a claim
Removal of the airframe from the operator’s traffic schedule
questions.value: Full irrevocable and unconditional payment of the agreed insurance value
questions.quote: paid irrevocably and unconditionally in full
questions.reason: §10.3 keeps both financing and periodic rent running until the payment condition is met.

questions.prompt: What further check precedes termination of the lease term under the whole-aircraft loss provision?
choices: All secured obligations have also been paid, discharged or performed
The operator has ordered a replacement aircraft
An engine has been removed from its mount
questions.value: All secured obligations have also been paid, discharged or performed
questions.quote: if all Secured Obligations have been paid, discharged, or performed
questions.reason: Conveyance also has its own joint written request mechanics. Engine-only loss follows another branch.

proof.prompt: Copy the words in the continuing-rent paragraph that tie the payment obligation to final settlement.
proof.start: (2) Until the date on which the Agreed Insurance Value is paid
proof.end: If the Agreed Insurance Value is paid irrevocably
proof.quote: paid irrevocably and unconditionally in full

memo: Keep both rent streams in the liquidity forecast. Confirm the payment due date, payee and actual application with the insurer and lessor. Reconcile any conditional refund of unaccrued rent separately, then clear remaining secured obligations before treating the lease term as ended.
